plan: v8: frozen re-test of the plan v7 full controllers on a fresh, larger blind set with a safety criterion relative to the classical baseline
written: 2026-10-20 ~22:05 JST, after the v7 full M3 verdict (2/5, not met) and before any v8 episode is flown; the v7 full M3 result stands and is reported unchanged
why_new_criterion: v7 full used "0 crashes" as an absolute bar. The classical opponent itself crashed in the v7 full blind set (1 of 96 episodes), so an absolute zero bar is stricter on the learned layer than on the baseline it is compared with. v8 asks for safety non-inferiority to the classical baseline on the same cases instead. This criterion was proposed after seeing the v7 full result (both learned crashes on one case, a height escape); that history is disclosed here.

controllers.note: exactly the centres selected in v7 full (no retraining, no reselection)
secondary_arms: mlp_ppo and mlp_bc (HomePC, the v7 full selected checkpoints)

tasks: bench9 evade / redirect / dash, scoring unchanged (score9 / score8)

blind.note: fresh: never flown by any controller before; generated by bench9.cases9

ratio: as v7 full: per case score / classical median of its task and direction class on this blind set; task ratio = mean over cases; average = mean of the 3 task ratios

primary_M4.per_seed: average ratio <= 0.95 AND number of crashed episodes <= the classical opponent's number of crashed episodes on the same 192 cases
primary_M4.overall: M4 holds if >= 3 of 5 seeds pass

secondary: crash rate of every arm with a 95% Clopper-Pearson interval
per task / per class ratios and paired wins
the v7 full M3 verdict reported alongside, unchanged
machine_rule: CloudPC-2 (reference) for snn_es, snn_bc and classical; HomePC for the PPO arms (bit-identical on bench9 selftest; 2 of 96 v7-full classical cases differ in the 4th decimal)
